extracted.intended_audience: Columbia University public affairs/communications staff, departmental communicators, and faculty interacting with media
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing and managing institutional press releases and media communications for Columbia University, covering what gets released, format/style, approvals, expert sourcing, timing, and special/legal considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate release topics
rubrics_metrics.description: What Columbia Releases: Major research findings; University statements on public issues; Awards and honors; Major hires; Significant programs; Crisis responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press releases should be limited to significant institutional news and events that warrant an official University statement or broad distribution; routine or minor items may not qualify. These releases are posted by the Office of Public Affairs from across the University.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to AP style
rubrics_metrics.description: Format Standards: AP style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write releases using Associated Press style conventions as the default editorial standard for punctuation, capitalization, dates, numbers, and general newsroom expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use university-approved boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: Format Standards: University-approved boilerplate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the official Columbia boilerplate (standard institutional description) at the end of releases to ensure consistent institutional branding and factual language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide standard contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Format Standards: Standard contact info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every release should include clear contact details (press office email/phone and relevant departmental or subject-matter contacts) so reporters can follow up; use the Office of Public Affairs' standard contact conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format faculty titles per Columbia style
rubrics_metrics.description: Format Standards: Faculty titles per Columbia style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Columbia's preferred conventions for formatting faculty titles and affiliations; verify accuracy of names, ranks, departments, and institutional units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate embargoes with journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Format Standards: Embargo coordination with journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When releasing research findings tied to journal publication, coordinate embargo timing with the journal and ensure compliance with embargo policies before publishing the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with University priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit Quality Rubric: Aligned with University priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Releases should advance or reflect Columbia's strategic priorities (including president and trustee priorities) and tell the University's story in ways consistent with institutional goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify relevant experts for interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit Quality Rubric: Identifies relevant experts available for interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure subject-matter experts are identified, available and prepared for media engagement; include expert contact information and availability in the release or via the media-relations process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide context and explain research importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit Quality Rubric: Provides context (research importance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the research or announcement matters—background, implications, and significance should be clear so reporters and the public understand the broader relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include links to journals and source materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit Quality Rubric: Includes journal links for studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicable, supply direct links to the underlying journal article, study materials, or primary sources; these should be accurate and respect embargo rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a standard press release format
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit Quality Rubric: Standard format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Office's established release structure (headline, dateline, lead, body, boilerplate, contacts) to maintain clarity and consistency across communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic timing of releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit Quality Rubric: Strategic timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan release timing strategically to maximize media pickup and align with institutional calendars, news cycles, partner timelines, and embargo agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate releases across departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit Quality Rubric: Coordinated across departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage relevant internal stakeholders (colleges, schools, Government and Community Affairs, legal, research offices) to ensure messaging alignment and prevent conflicting communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal review for university statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Special Considerations: University statements require legal review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain legal review for official University statements, particularly those addressing contentious public issues or matters with potential legal exposure, before release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow crisis communications protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Special Considerations: Crisis communications follow specific protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In crises, activate designated crisis-communication procedures and chains of approval; crisis messaging should be coordinated, timely, and led by authorized officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain consent for faculty quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Special Considerations: Faculty quotes require consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure explicit consent from faculty before publishing direct quotes attributed to them; confirm exact wording and attribution to avoid disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose IP and grant information where relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Special Considerations: IP/grant disclosures included where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include disclosures about intellectual property, licensing, and funding sources/grants that materially relate to the research or announcement, per institutional policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media inquiries routing
rubrics_metrics.description: Press email for institutional inquiries; direct contact for non-institutional issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Office of Public Affairs press email as the central routing point for institutional media inquiries and provide direct departmental contacts for specialized or non-institutional issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain an experts-for-media directory
rubrics_metrics.description: Experts for the Media: Columbia maintains a regularly-updated resource that connects reporters with university experts categorized by topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the media-expert resource current and categorized; use it proactively to match reporters with appropriate Columbia experts for news-driven coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice and audience orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications Function: Voice of Columbia globally; reaches diverse audiences (media, neighbors, government, alumni).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft messaging in a voice that represents Columbia institutionally and is accessible to diverse audiences; tailor tone and emphasis for target audiences (media, community, government, alumni) while preserving institutional voice.
